summary: Steel lookout on Woonsocket Hill, North Smithfield, RI: NHLR dates it 1926, local reporting 1956; town-owned since 1990, unstaffed, restoration funded in 2025.

access.note: Road up the hill is privately owned; town owns the ground beneath the tower; no signed directions (2015 Register visit); fence often cut (local account)

events.note: 1923 state report: three new stations set up that year, making five; Woonsocket Hill is among the five, and the towers range 40 to 68 feet. The report does not say whether Woonsocket Hill was one of the three new stations; unclear whether this is the standing tower
NHLR 'Built' field; repeated by a 2025 report
1954-55 state report recommends new cabs for Woonsocket Hill and Shannock towers, which had become unsafe for observers
Local account: state replaced the wooden structure with the present steel tower; 'Built in 1956' per NRI NOW (2021)
State sold the tower to North Smithfield under a recreation grant program
Registered June 23, 2009 as US 807, RI 3; nominated by Henry Isenberg
Register visit April 6, 2015: good overall condition; needs paint and minor window repair; not staffed
Town council allocated $68,382 for repair and restoration, added to a previous $2,500 budget
State EMA finished a 140-foot monopole beside the tower; state antennas removed from the tower; restoration work funded

corrections.proposed: Town of North Smithfield (owner since 1990); the Register still lists RI DEM as administrator
corrections.why: The local account says the state sold the tower to North Smithfield in 1990. The Register's administrator line predates or ignores that sale; the 2025 report still shows state antennas on the site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and a 2025 report give 1926. A 1923 state report says three new stations were set up that year, making five, and lists Woonsocket Hill among them. Local reporting and a 2021 report give 1956 for the present steel tower and describe an older wooden tower moved from Cato Hill in the 1920s. The sources read do not settle the date of the standing tower; the story reports the disagreement.

The 2015 Register visit says 'Tower is maintained by a local fire department', while the 2021 local report says no one maintains the accompanying building. Both are reported as stated; the story does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Build date is genuinely contested: NHLR and a 2025 report say 1926; a 1923 state report says three new stations were set up that year, making five, with Woonsocket Hill among them; local reporting and a 2021 report say 1956 for the present steel tower. Kept as a disagreement, not resolved. Ownership: the brief's RI DEM agency comes from NHLR; the local account says the state sold the tower to North Smithfield in 1990. Proposed as a correction (agency). Access 'restricted' is a judgment from the private road, no signs and cut fence; no official access statement was read. Staffing 'unstaffed' rests on the April 2015 Register visit only. Restoration status: the 2025 report says work was funded; a search result (not read, budget used) suggests a later restoration; the editor should check before any claim that restoration is complete. A 1953 vandalism item on the Forest Lookouts page cites a Zanesville, Ohio newspaper and an observer named Ariel Mowry; its location is unclear, so it is not used. No notable fire found in the pages read. Height 19.8 m from the NHLR 65-foot figure. Elevation: NHLR 569 ft (173 m). The Breeze article date is not in the text read.
